title: Proactive Audit
hook: Your systems didn't break overnight. They drifted a little every week while you weren't looking.
statement: Inspect and fine-tune your systems regularly, before small drift turns into a big fix.
explainer: Each little slip feels too small to bother with. But drift stacks up over time, so a system you ignore for a year needs way more work than one you check monthly.
sop: Put recurring reviews on the calendar, monthly for business, weekly for personal.
Compare what's actually happening to what the system was built to do.
Score Drift from 1 to 10 and note the Time since your last check.
Make one fix per review, not a full overhaul.
Log what you found so drift is something you see, not just feel.
equation_example: Drift 6, Time 8 months. 6 × 8 = 48, so Health is 1 ÷ 48, about 0.02. Catch it at 1 month: 6 × 1 = 6, so Health is 1 ÷ 6, about 0.17. Higher means it still runs as designed. Lower means drift's piling up.
question: Pick the one system you've been meaning to tune up and put a review on your calendar this week.
closing_statement: Drift always costs more the longer you let it sit.
